title: Journalists visit COESP and bolster the response to Mpox in Angola - WHO | Regional Office for Africa

analysis.time: The event date is 5 October 2026. The publication date is 6 October 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: The event took place in Angola, specifically in Luanda, where the Public Health Emergency Operations Center (COESP) is located. The affected population includes the general public and health authorities in Angola.
analysis.event: Journalists visited the Public Health Emergency Operations Center (COESP) in Luanda to bolster the response to the Mpox outbreak. This was reported by the WHO Regional Office for Africa.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: As of 2024, Angola has reported 796 confirmed cases and two deaths from Mpox. The disease can cause serious complications in vulnerable populations, and early detection, contact tracing, and communication are crucial to limiting transmission.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The WHO continues to support the Ministry of Health in strengthening epidemiological surveillance, risk communication, and coordination mechanisms for the Mpox response. The visit to COESP aimed to enhance public understanding and reduce misinformation.

analysis.brief_en: In Angola, journalists visited the Public Health Emergency Operations Center (COESP) in Luanda on 5 October 2026 as part of efforts to bolster the response to the Mpox outbreak. The WHO Regional Office for Africa reported that the country has recorded 796 confirmed cases and two deaths since 2024. The visit aimed to improve risk communication and public access to reliable information about the disease. The COESP plays a central role in coordinating the national response by analyzing epidemiological data and guiding decisions on case investigation, vaccination, treatment, and community engagement. The WHO continues to support Angola's health authorities in strengthening surveillance and communication strategies to control the outbreak. Mpox, a viral disease transmitted through close contact, can lead to serious complications in vulnerable groups, emphasizing the need for early detection and accurate public messaging.

analysis.time: The outbreak was declared over in December 2025, with the analysis covering a database extract frozen on 1 July 2026. The temporal signal showed a sharp rise in notifications from April 2025, peaking at 37 laboratory-confirmed paediatric cases in the epidemiological week ending 18 May 2025, and declining through June with a smaller resurgence in September and early October. The publication date is 2026-10-09.
analysis.location_and_population: The outbreak occurred in Sierra Leone, specifically concentrated in Western Area Urban, the densely populated district containing the capital Freetown. The affected population included children younger than 15 years, with 415 cases recorded. The geographic distribution also included northern districts such as Koinadugu and Falaba.
analysis.event: A retrospective national study published in PLOS Neglected Tropical Diseases documented 415 children younger than 15 years among 5,466 cases with recorded age, meaning children accounted for 7.6 percent of the outbreak’s known burden. The study found that the clade IIb G.1 virus had been transmitting locally before public detection, and the paediatric epidemic curve was a mirror of the national outbreak, amplified through domestic contact networks.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Of the 415 paediatric cases, 411 were laboratory-confirmed, four were classified as probable, and none were clinician-diagnosed only. The age distribution was strikingly young, with 188 children aged 0 to 4 years (45.3 percent) and 230 of the 415 children being male. Three children died, resulting in a case fatality proportion of 1.1 percent. The authors caution that these rates may be overestimated due to potential underestimation of paediatric denominators in northern districts.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The research team, led by investigators at Sierra Leone’s National Public Health Agency, used the national District Health Information Software 2 database and enriched it with patient charts and outbreak-investigation forms. The authors emphasize the need for district-specific age denominators and testing data to accurately interpret geographic differences. They also stress the importance of distinguishing admission purpose and standardizing documentation of severity, treatment, complications, and recovery.

Three children died, resulting in a case fatality proportion of 1.1 percent, with delayed presentation and poor feeding or dehydration noted in the fatal cases. The authors stress the need for improved surveillance and standardized documentation to better understand the outbreak’s impact on children and ensure adequate care.

The latest case involved a 29-year-old man who developed symptoms on September 28 and was isolated at Princess Margaret Hospital. All 21 patients reported engaging in high-risk sexual behavior, including unprotected sex with multiple partners or strangers. Genetic analysis revealed some cases shared identical sequences, suggesting a common source and multiple transmission chains among men who have sex with men. The CHP emphasized the importance of keeping sexual partner contact details for effective contact tracing and prevention. Most patients had not been vaccinated, and the center is continuing its investigation and will report to the World Health Organization.

analysis.time: The UK Health Security Agency’s mpox surveillance update was published on 8 October 2026, and the data covers cases through 30 September 2026. The September figures refer to the month commencing 1 September 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: The data focuses on the UK, with London being central to England’s regional picture. The affected population includes men who have sex with men, particularly in London, and cases are distributed across England, Northern Ireland, Scotland, and Wales.
analysis.event: The UK Health Security Agency updated its mpox surveillance data, noting that clade Ib has become more common than clade IIb in the country. The report highlights an epidemiological shift with clade Ib case numbers increasing and surpassing clade IIb from July 2026.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: From 6 May 2022 to 30 September 2026, the UK recorded 5,023 mpox cases, including 226 classified as clade Ib and 972 as clade IIb in the period from 2023 to September 2026. For September 2026 alone, England reported 46 clade Ib cases, three clade IIb cases, and 19 cases with an unknown clade. The surveillance data does not establish individual risk levels but indicates a shift in clade prevalence.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The UK Health Security Agency revised its reporting format in August 2026 to separate confirmed clade Ib, confirmed clade IIb, recombinant clades, and cases with unknown clades. The data is a surveillance snapshot, not real-time, and may include corrections from delayed reporting or updated patient information. The report emphasizes that the figures should not be interpreted as a precise local count for London.

While the national figures show London as central to the regional pattern, no specific September London case count is provided. The surveillance data is a snapshot and may include corrections. The report also mentions London’s prominence in vaccination efforts, with 63,624 first doses and 42,902 second doses administered to men who have sex with men by 31 March 2026. The figures do not establish individual risk levels but reflect an epidemiological trend. The revised reporting format aims to clarify clade classifications and improve data comparability across reports.

analysis.time: The event date is 28th September 2026, with the patient's symptoms noticed on 8th October 2026. The publication date is 10th October 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: The case occurred in Hong Kong, specifically in Mong Kok. The affected population includes a 29-year-old man and other high-risk individuals, particularly men who have sex with men, who have engaged in high-risk sexual activities.
analysis.event: A 29-year-old man was diagnosed with Mpox after attending an outreach vaccination service in Mong Kok. The Centre for Health Protection confirmed the case, and the patient was isolated and treated at Princess Margaret Hospital.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Since 2022, Hong Kong has recorded 114 Mpox cases, all male, with 30 reported in 2026 alone. Of these, 23 are local cases and seven have been imported. The outbreak is linked to high-risk sexual practices, with many patients having found casual male partners using dating applications and most having not previously received the Mpox vaccine. The Centre for Health Protection has increased prevention and response measures.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The Centre for Health Protection is continuing its investigation and will notify the World Health Organization of the case. They have expanded vaccination services, established new vaccination sites, and increased public education efforts. Authorities are urging the public to retain contact information for sexual partners to facilitate contact tracing.

analysis.brief_en: A 29-year-old man in Hong Kong has been diagnosed with Mpox after attending an outreach vaccination service in Mong Kok. The Centre for Health Protection confirmed the case, and the patient was isolated and treated at Princess Margaret Hospital. The patient developed a papule on his buttock on 28th September, with subsequent rashes, fever, and swollen lymph nodes. His symptoms were noticed on 8th October during the vaccination service. The diagnosis is part of a larger recent increase in Mpox cases in the city, with 30 cases reported in 2026 alone. Of these, 23 are local cases, and 7 have been imported. The outbreak is linked to high-risk sexual activities, with many patients having found casual male partners through dating apps and not previously vaccinated. The Centre for Health Protection has increased prevention and response measures, including expanding vaccination services and establishing new sites. They have also urged the public to retain contact information for sexual partners to aid contact tracing. The authorities are working with online dating platforms to promote safe practices and vaccination information within the community.
